To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the phase fluctuations of the superconducting order parameter are important for the normal and superfluid properties of the 2D system, in particular the non-Fermi-liquid properties, and that the pseudogap behavior can be understood as the result of the dynamical fluctuations of the superfluid order parameter.

we have studied the effect of static phase fluctuations on the normal state properties of a two dimensional system with attractive interaction and found that the system has non-Fermi Liquid properties.

1) the phase fluctuations of the order parameter in 2D systems with short-range attraction give rise to non-Fermi-liquid behavior, 2) these phase fluctuations are responsible for the observed pseudogaps in 2D superconductors and in the normal state of the high temperature superconductors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a 2D model of a superconductor with attractive four- fermion interaction.
the study of the phase fluctuations in 2D superconductor and the resultant effects on the single particle and collective excitations.
a study of the phase fluctuations in the order parameter and the effect of these phase fluctuations on the single-particle properties of the system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2D fermion system is a non-Fermi-liquid with a pseudogap at low temperatures
the 2D system is not a superconductor in the strict sense of the word, but a non-Fermi-liquid.
the phase fluctuation theory is able to account for a number of observed non-Fermi-liquid properties of high-temperature superconductors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the phase fluctuations of the order parameter are responsible for the non-Fermi-liquid behaviour of 2D superconductors.
the phase fluctuations in the superconducting order parameter lead to the non-Fermi-liquid properties of the normal state of the 2D superconductor.
the 2D Fermi system with attraction is a non-Fermi-liquid and the superconducting properties are dominated by phase fluctuations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
static fluctuations of the order parameter can be used to understand the non-Fermi-liquid properties of the pseudogap phase in the 2D Fermi-system with attraction.
phase fluctuations are the main reason for pseudogap behaviour in 2D systems.
a 2D Fermi system with an attractive interaction has non-Fermi Liquid properties.
